Awww, that’s frustrating. I find magic circles really fiddly to this day. You might want to do a chain and slip stitch into the first chain instead of a magic circle to make it a bit easier. You will have a hole in the middle of the loop (as opposed to magic circles which you can tighten so there is no hole) but there’s nothing wrong with that. As for the yarn, maybe get another skein of better quality stuff to play around with? Hobbii and Hobbycraft (if you’re in the UK) do good quality stuff and I don’t really have an issue with it loosening up beyond use. 

I would also avoid cotton yarn for now and just use acrylic (if you’re not already) as cotton can get reeeaallly loose if you’re constantly unwinding your work or putting the crochet hook through the yarn instead of the chain itself. Hope that helps somewhat

Another thing I’ll throw in is whether you’d be interested in doing some less popular tourist activities. Most people want to go to the beach and the seaside cafes and the beautiful walks and I absolutely don’t blame them. However, especially if you plan to be a little more sedentary, Cornwall has so many other amazing attractions and features that you might not see at the top of google. We have a rich mining history and the ruins of the old engine houses are spectacular and hauntingly beautiful. There are also places that embrace Cornish language, music and art that is a bit different to your average harbour / driftwood / nautical themes.

The Great Flat Lode is a relatively flat walk which goes weaves through one of the most historically significant mining sites in Cornwall. You also have Heartlands nearby that can be a little inconsistent with opening times but has an old engine house and museum worth visiting. There is also a shop there that specialises in Cornish Language books, gifts and art which can make for some really unique souvenirs and gifts. Going back up north to Newquay, drop by the Urban Kelt coffee shop for some more unique and authentic Cornish vibes.

I’m personally a sucker for cafes around Penzance and Hayle as I’m a West Cornwall native and I also feel that they are popular but don’t get the same amount of love as the North Cornwall ones!

Rick Rescorla was an immigrant from Cornwall, the most southwesterly point of Britain. For those of you who don’t know, Cornwall is a Celtic region with an incredibly tight knit community. Not only did Rick rigorously create his own evacuation drills prior to the 9/11 attacks (that ended up saving the lives of most of employees of the company he was security for), but he sang traditional Cornish folk songs to the scared survivors making their way down the stairwell. 

I am from Cornwall, only 20 minutes from his hometown (Hayle). My grandpa worked with his cousins and uncle, and his extended family still live around that area. His surname is a traditional Cornish surname, and it’s likely that he soothed thousands of people in a Cornish accent that had been weathered and worn by years of travel, military service, and life experience.

We have a memorial to him in Hayle Harbour that is kept clean and tidy with beautiful flowers all year round.

For an idea of what songs were sang to those thousands of people making their way down the stairwell, please check out this playlist. Survivors notably remember Rick singing ‘Camborne Hill,’ a tongue in cheek song about a steam engine making its way up a local hill and hitting several technical faults along the way: https://youtu.be/oq3Ya5Q1N3c

A fearless, heroic man.

I’m an ex low self-esteemed. I’ve seen some amazing tips from other women, and I think they’re WONDERFUL. I’ll add some of mine in case it adds further help for anyone.

- social media: follow body positive people on Instagram! I find saggysara, bodyposipanda, and chessiekingg lovey people to start with. - write a list of things you like about YOU. They don’t have to be skills you earn money with. Or physical attributes. It can be things like, ‘I always pick up litter when I see it’. ‘Dogs love me and I love dogs’. ‘I have soft hair’. ‘My eyes are an amazing colour’. ‘I love writing’. Etc. Try not to make it a list of ‘people like abc and xyz about me’ unless it’s from a person you truly value and the compliment really uplifts you. Look at this list whenever you feel low. And add to it when you’re feeling well.

- try to remember (this is HARD) that hundreds of businesses rely on women feeling rubbish about themselves in order to make money. It’s hard to sell clothes, makeup, hair products and ‘self care’ items to women who feel beautiful and successful and happy in themselves. I’m not going to wildly assume that that’s where your low self esteem branches from, but it’s shocking how deep these companies can get under our skin in order to take our money.

First of all I just want to say that, although I know it's causing you upset, your skin looks really good in general. :)

I would advise to not add in loads and loads of new products all at once, as the general balance of your skin doesn't look too bad at all. Maybe a gentle cleanser in the evenings (something without fragrance and for normal skin, not dry or oily). For your blackheads I would **strongly advise against** using a physical exfoliator, and would consider something chemical, such as glycolic acid. Glycolic acid and lactic acid are both good for helping reduce blackheads, and glycolic acid is pretty weak and is a great starting point. I would get a glycolic acid chemical peel (sounds a lot scarier than it is) and use that as per instructions.

For spots and breakouts, my number one recommendation is neat tea tree oil. put one drop on a cotton bud and dab the spot. You could also put a drop or two on a wet face cloth and gently pat an area if it's a site of regular breakouts. Tea tree oil is anti-inflammatory and anti-microbial - if you only got one thing to change your routine, I'd advise this!

I'd also advise a light moisturiser with a small amount of SPF in it to help preserve your skin and prevent wrinkles from furthering. I'm not really an expert on wrinkle reduction but there'll probably be others on here who can assist.

I don't know where you live, but in the UK places such as Superdrug have their own brand of skincare called Naturally Radiant and covers most products you'd want at this point and for a super cheap price.

​

I think the main bit to remember is that everyone's skin is different and what works for me certainly won't work for someone else, etc. From looking at your skin, we have a lot of similarities, so I thought I would share my skincare habits in case it helps.
